field-type.note: Type colour on every colour field, in both themes. Never re-tinted.

pass-green.note: Same value as module ink 3. Always paired with a caps label.

fail-red.note: Same value as module ink 7; equals the accent in dark theme.

module-ultramarine.usedFor: Module 1 in both courses; the Software Sense course accent; the landing specimen field.

module-teal.usedFor: Module 2; the tip and "Ask your AI" callout ink.

module-rust.usedFor: Module 4; The Agentic Coding Course accent.

display.purpose: One enormous numeral in the landing specimen field. One per site.

display-sm.purpose: The same numeral device at course scale, in the monograph head's ink field.

headline.purpose: The page h1. Balanced wrapping, capped at 24-26ch on head blocks.

title.purpose: Every h2. Always carries a 1px ink rule above it — the section break is a printed rule.

subhead.purpose: h3. Goes uppercase at 0.06-0.09em tracking inside a card or column.

dek.purpose: The standfirst under an h1 — the only grotesque set at weight 400. Capped at 54ch.

body.purpose: Charter running text, held to a 64ch measure everywhere.

label.purpose: All furniture: spec keys, plate numbers, table headings, captions, callout labels, rail section heads.

kicker.purpose: Accent-coloured line above an h1 naming the angle. Loosest tracking in the system.

action-sm.purpose: Row buttons inside a ruled action strip.

data.purpose: A measured value sitting under its caps key — spec numbers, a figure's headline figure.

mono.purpose: Code only, on Sheet Tint inside a hairline.

shadows.name: inset-state-bar
shadows.purpose: 3px vertical bar inside a quiz option's left edge marking correct (or --bad for wrong), without changing the box size. Blur 0 — a drawn rule.

shadows.name: inset-current-underline
shadows.purpose: Active-page marker inside the sticky nav, where a border would shift the row. Blur 0.

shadows.name: inset-focus-fill
shadows.purpose: The search field's focus treatment, thickening inward instead of growing. Blur 0.

shadows.name: shared-cell-outline
shadows.purpose: 2x2 matrix cell seams; adjacent outlines overlap exactly so every seam stays one hairline wide. Heavy variant: 0 0 0 3px <ink> for the loaded quadrant. Blur 0.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Every hover/focus state change in the system — background, colour, border-colour.

motion.name: dim
motion.purpose: Knowledge-map opacity dimming to 12% when a node or module is isolated.

motion.name: ease-authored
motion.purpose: The one authored easing: the field wipe and the progress bar's scaleX.

motion.name: wipe
motion.purpose: clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0) -> inset(0 0 0 0) with animation-fill-mode: backwards. Staggered 0.14s / 0.24s for the two course cards. Content is never animated.

motion.name: progress
motion.purpose: transform: scaleX() on a progress fill — re-runs on every mark-complete click, so it must not animate width.

layout.name: measure
layout.purpose: The running-text line length. Never widened, whatever the container.

layout.name: gut
layout.purpose: The figure gutter to the right of the text column.

layout.name: frame
layout.purpose: The outer frame for full-bleed heads, the map plate, and the lesson sheet.

layout.name: wide-container
layout.purpose: Index pages that carry grids; their prose children are re-capped to the measure.

narrative.overview:
This is a Geigy-Basel product monograph (1953-72) rendered as static HTML: white stock, printing-ink hairlines, tight Helvetica caps for every piece of furniture, and a serif — Charter — reserved for running text. It is aimed at a professional with four spare minutes, and the ambition is that the sheet is precise enough and well set enough that people keep it. Diagrams are not illustrations dropped into prose; they are the architecture, and every one is a numbered plate.

The world is deliberately flat. There is no radius anywhere in the two stylesheets and no blurred shadow anywhere in the two stylesheets. Depth is a ruled line: a 3px heavy rule opens a block, a 1px ink hairline separates the things inside it, a 1px soft hairline separates the rows within those. Colour arrives at page scale — a module's ink fills a whole panel and carries white type — never as a small tinted chip. The one authored moment of motion is a flat colour field wiping down the way a press lays ink; the text is on screen from the first frame regardless.

Two things are explicitly refused. The modern documentation site: no sidebar tree, no thin sans, no blue links. And the site's own former identity: no cream paper, no serif display, no terracotta essay column. Where the build and the direction contract diverge, the build is the record — the contract says diagrams are the architecture, and the vocabulary is complete (eleven diagram types), but only 24 numbered plates exist across the 60 lesson pages so far. The vocabulary is the system; the coverage is still growing.
keyCharacteristics: White sheet, printing-ink hairlines, zero radius, zero blur.
Elevation is a ruled line — 3px heavy, 1px ink, 1px soft.
Seven module inks as page-scale fields carrying #ffffff type.
Furniture in 0.6rem Helvetica caps at 0.11-0.18em tracking; running text in Charter at 64ch.
Every figure is a numbered plate inside a ruled frame.
Interactive furniture inverts to solid ink on hover in 0.12s.
System font stacks only, no external request of any kind, works in print.

rules.name: The Field Rule
rules.body: A module ink appears one of two ways: as a page-scale field with #ffffff type on it, or as type on the white sheet through its t variant. It is never a small tinted chip behind dark text. The one licensed exception is a wash — color-mix(in srgb, <ink> 10-22%, var(--paper)) under body ink, used for the loaded quadrant of a 2x2 and the shaded band of a scale. A wash is a region; a chip is a badge. Badges are the rejected world.

rules.name: The Two-Way AA Rule
rules.body: An ink joins the palette only if it is legible in both directions against the sheet: white type on the field, and the ink itself as type on white. Every current module ink measures >=5.79:1 against #ffffff (min: Teal at 5.79, max: Ultramarine at 9.98), and every dark-theme t variant measures >=7.09:1 against #0f1017. This replaced a pastel-pill palette that failed; it is load-bearing, not taste.

rules.name: The Furniture Floor Rule
rules.body: Ink Furniture on Sheet Tint measures exactly 4.50:1 — the AA minimum for text under 18.66px, which is all of it. That pair is the floor of the system. Do not lighten Ink Furniture, do not darken Sheet Tint, and do not introduce a third grey between them.

rules.name: The Borrowed Semantics Rule
rules.body: Pass Green is module ink 3, Fail Red is module ink 7, and in dark theme the academy accent and the fail ink are the same value. Hue therefore never carries pass/fail on its own — the caps label (RED FLAGS TO CATCH, COMPLETE) is what says it. Never build a state that is distinguishable only by colour.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Charter sets running text. The grotesque sets everything that is furniture — labels, spec strips, plate numbers, tables, captions, deks, headings, buttons, the whole route rail, and all text inside a figure. There is no third voice except code. If you cannot say which of the two a new element is, it is furniture.

rules.name: The Caps Furniture Rule
rules.body: Furniture is 0.585-0.68rem, weight 700, uppercase, tracked 0.11-0.18em. At that size tighter tracking prints as a smudge and looser prints as a logo. Never set furniture in lowercase and never below 0.585rem.

rules.name: The Tightening Rule
rules.body: Negative tracking scales with size: -0.014em at dek, -0.028em at h1/h2, -0.035em at a data value, -0.06em at the specimen numeral. No grotesque display line is set at normal tracking.

rules.name: The System Stack Rule
rules.body: System font stacks only. No webfont, no @font-face, no external request — not now, not for one page. The fallback chains are the design.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Running text holds 64ch. A page may be as wide as it needs to be; a line may not. Widening a container is never a reason to widen prose.

rules.name: The Local Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: There is no global breakpoint ladder. Each component collapses at the width its own content actually breaks — 520/560/620px for diagrams and furniture, 640/680px for the map and step chains, 760/820px for the two head blocks, 1080px where the lesson rail becomes a horizontal strip, 1180px where the figure gutter opens. Do not invent a shared sm/md/lg scale to tidy this up; the numbers are content measurements.

rules.name: The Ruled-Line Rule
rules.body: Elevation is a ruled line. If something needs to read as raised, separate, or new, give it a heavier rule — never a shadow, never a gradient, never a lift on hover.

rules.name: The Zero-Blur Rule
rules.body: box-shadow is permitted only with a blur radius of exactly 0, as a drawn rule that a border cannot produce. Any blur value, any filter: drop-shadow, any spread meant to read as glow belongs to the world this one refuses.

rules.name: The Print Fallback Rule
rules.body: Every colour field must still read when its background is dropped. In print the whole token set re-declares to black on white and every field — pill, course card head, module header, specimen block, rail block — becomes a white box with a 1px black border. A new field-carrying component is not finished until it has a print rule.

rules.name: The Inversion Rule
rules.body: Interactive furniture inverts on hover: background becomes Printing Ink, text becomes Sheet White, over 0.12s. That single gesture covers nav links, buttons, search results, prev/next cells, table-of-contents entries, quiz options, map controls, and legend items. Never a tint, never a lift, never a radius, never a colour change to something new.

rules.name: The Field-Follows-Page Rule
rules.body: --field on the body element is the only per-page identity declaration, and every accented component reads it with a fallback (var(--field, var(--ink))). Setting it once recolours the rail block, the module pill, the plate rules, the progress fills, the step numerals, the diagram inks, and the current-section marker together. Figures may override with --f; landing course cards use --course-accent. Never hard-code a module hex into a component.

rules.name: The Text-Variant Rule
rules.body: When a module ink is used as a field, use the base ink (--m1...--m7). When it is used as type or as a thin stroke on the sheet, use the text variant (--m1t...--m7t), which is identical in light theme and re-tinted lighter in dark theme. A base ink used as type goes muddy on the dark sheet.

rules.name: The One Authored Moment Rule
rules.body: Motion is one gesture: a colour field wipes down from clip-path: inset(0 0 100% 0) with animation-fill-mode: backwards, 0.5-0.62s on cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1), staggered 0.14s and 0.24s for the two course cards. Content is never animated and is visible on the first frame, so nothing can be left invisible if the animation never runs. State changes are 0.12s. The progress bar animates transform: scaleX() rather than width, because it re-runs on every mark-complete click. Everything is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

dos: Do put a module ink on screen as a page-scale field with #ffffff type, or as type through its --mNt variant. Nothing in between.
Do open every new block with a 3px rule and divide its interior with 1px hairlines: heavy rule -> ink hairline -> soft hairline.
Do read the page's identity from var(--field, var(--ink)) (or --f in a figure, --course-accent on a landing card) so one body declaration recolours the whole page.
Do set every label, key, caption, plate number, table heading, and button in the grotesque at 0.585-0.68rem, weight 700, uppercase, tracked 0.11-0.18em.
Do hold running text to 64ch, whatever the container width, and re-cap prose children individually on wide index pages.
Do invert interactive furniture to solid ink on hover in 0.12s.
Do wrap every figure in a .fig plate so it gets a number, a caption, and a rule in the page's ink.
Do check a new ink both ways against the sheet — >=4.5:1 for white type on it and for it as type on white — plus its dark-theme variant against #0f1017.
Do give every field-carrying component a print rule that drops the background to white and outlines the box in 1px black.
Do pair every status colour with a caps label that says the same thing.
donts: Don't set border-radius anywhere. Not on a button, not on an input, not on a map node. The value is 0 and it is the world.
Don't use a blurred shadow, a drop-shadow filter, a gradient meant to read as depth, or a hover lift. box-shadow is allowed only at blur 0, as a drawn rule.
Don't render a module ink as a small pastel chip behind dark text. A 10-22% color-mix wash under body ink across a region is the only tinted use.
Don't add a webfont, an icon font, a CDN stylesheet, or any external asset request. System stacks and inline SVG only.
Don't set body copy in the grotesque, or furniture in the serif. There is no third family except monospace for code.
Don't lighten Ink Furniture or darken Sheet Tint — that pair already sits exactly at 4.50:1, the AA floor.
Don't hard-code a module hex inside a component's CSS; read --field/--f.
Don't distinguish any state by hue alone — Pass Green is also module ink 3, Fail Red is also module ink 7, and in dark theme the accent equals the fail ink.
Don't animate content in or out. Only a colour field moves, and the text under it is on screen from frame one.
Don't introduce a global sm/md/lg breakpoint scale. Breakpoints are per-component content measurements.
Don't build a sidebar tree, a thin-sans docs shell, or blue underlined links; and don't reintroduce cream paper, a serif display face, or terracotta.
